channel.title: US Top News and Analysis
channel.description: CNBC is the world leader in business news and real-time financial market coverage. Find fast, actionable information.

item.title: Dow leaps 1,000 points fueled by earnings, hopes for Hormuz Strait deal; S&P 500 hits record: Live updates
item.description: Stocks rose on Tuesday as oil prices dropped amid optimism that a U.S.-Iran deal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz could be on the horizon.

item.title: SpaceX earnings live updates: First report since IPO comes ahead of massive share unlock
item.description: Follow SpaceX’s Q2 2026 earnings live, with updates on revenue, Starlink, AI spending, Starship, guidance and SPCX stock.

item.title: Jeff Bezos just filed to sell $4 billion in Amazon. The shares are falling
item.description: The filing came after Amazon climbed to an all-time high on Monday, extending gains sparked by last week's quarterly results.

item.title: Stocks making the biggest moves midday: Palantir, Amazon, SpaceX, Sandisk, Snap & more
item.description: Here are some of the companies making headlines in midday trading.

item.title: Procter & Gamble will acquire supplements brand Thorne for $3.8 billion, CEO tells CNBC
item.description: P&G CEO Shailesh Jejurikar said the acquisition is a play to grow the company's health business on CNBC's "Squawk on the Street."

item.title: SK Hynix U.S. shares will double in the next 12 months, Cantor Fitzgerald says
item.description: While Cantor is the most bullish on SK Hynix stock, it's not alone in its zeal.

item.title: New Jersey sues Amazon on antitrust grounds, alleging it unlawfully wielded its power over delivery contractors
item.description: The complaint alleges Amazon's third-party delivery model leads to lower wages, unfair working conditions and a lack of competition.

item.title: Blanche approved by Judiciary Committee, sending Trump's AG nominee to full Senate vote
item.description: Attorney General nominee Todd Blanche will still need to receive 50 votes on the Senate floor to be confirmed after clearing the Senate Judiciary Committee.

item.title: Palantir jumps 27% on 'otherworldly' commercial revenue — here's what's driving the demand
item.description: "Our customers have declined to become vassal states of the language labs," Palantir's co-founder and CEO Alex Karp said after blowout second-quarter earnings.

item.title: Abdul El-Sayed, Haley Stevens square off Tuesday in Michigan Democratic primary
item.description: Michigan's Senate Democratic primary between Abdul El-Sayed and Rep. Haley Stevens is one of the most closely watched races of the midterm election.

item.title: How the 'Baby iPhone' and an Apple supplier leak explain China's recent supply chain moves
item.description: In China's biggest electronics marketplace, Huaqiangbei, technicians don't have the parts to make exact copies of Apple's latest phones.

item.title: Why Michigan voters are hearing 'communist' as they vote Tuesday
item.description: President Donald Trump and Republican allies are escalating attacks that label Democrats communists after progressive candidates won elections and primaries.

item.title: Why Ford believes its 10.2% July U.S. sales decline was still a 'good' month
item.description: The July decline adds to a lackluster sales year for the automaker, with results off 9.7% compared with 2025.

item.title: Polymarket in talks for fundraising round at more than $20 billion valuation
item.description: The reports come after the company told CNBC in June that its annualized revenue was well above $1 billion.

item.title: Apple shares downgraded due to memory chip inflation
item.description: Phillip Capital downgraded the iPhone manufacturer, saying the sharp rise in memory prices will undercut that momentum.

item.title: AMD earnings are a key test for chips and momentum stocks. Here's what the options market is saying
item.description: As AMD prepares to report earnings Tuesday after the bell, market participants face a divergence between positive earnings results and negative price action.

item.title: Philadelphia Fed President Paulson content with rates at current level, but keeping an open mind
item.description: Paulson said voting with the majority last week wasn't a tough decision.

item.title: Foreigners are buying fewer U.S. properties, but luxury homebuilders still draw them in
item.description: Foreign buyers are pulling back sharply from U.S. residential real estate, in part due to a pullback among workers that would qualify for H-1B visas.

item.title: Someone on Wall Street thinks SpaceX could triple this week
item.description: SpaceX reports its first earnings results since its June IPO Tuesday after the bell.

item.title: McDonald's names company veteran Skye Anderson as its U.S. president as growth in its largest market slows
item.description: McDonald's new U.S. President Skye Anderson has been with the company for 26 years and succeeds Joe Erlinger in the role.

item.title: Jim Cramer weighs the next move after massive rallies in two tech stocks
item.description: The Investing Club holds its "Morning Meeting" every weekday at 10:20 a.m. ET.

item.title: Chase Bank new account bonuses: Earn up to $3,000
item.description: Chase is offering cash incentives for new checking, savings and credit card customers. See how you can earn up to $3,000 and enjoy other account benefits.

item.title: The internet's grandma & granddaughter advice duo on dating, marriage and family
item.description: To recognize the country’s 250th year, CNBC Make It got notable voices in politics, finance and relationships across age ranges to sit down and spark conversation about what it means to achieve happiness and success in this country today. Kim Murstein, 30, the founder and co-host of the "Excuse My Grandma" podcast, spoke with Gail Rudnick, 84, her grandmother and podcast co-host.

item.title: Bessent says U.S. backed Japan’s yen intervention to help stabilize Asia
item.description: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said the U.S. bought yen alongside Japan to curb currency volatility and reduce risks to Asian markets.

item.title: Wayfair stock jumps more than 25% as retailer posts strongest U.S. growth since 2020
item.description: Wayfair, a pandemic darling that's seen sales slow since lockdown orders were lifted, posted its strongest U.S. growth since 2020 during its second quarter.

item.title: McDonald's says its U.S. business is falling short as it announces new head of its largest market
item.description: McDonald's stock has fallen more than 11% this year, dragging its market cap down to roughly $191 billion.

item.title: Pfizer tops estimates, hikes low end of revenue guidance on strength of Eliquis, other drugs
item.description: Pfizer said it cut its full-year revenue expectation for its Covid products to $4 billion, down from around $5 billion previously.

item.title: Caterpillar lifts 2026 sales growth target on strong data center demand after quarterly profit beat
item.description: The industrial equipment giant has seen a surge in orders for construction equipment amid a nationwide buildout of data centers.

item.title: Merck hikes revenue outlook as new drug sales grow, but cuts profit guidance due to deal charges
item.description: Merck cut its profit guidance due to a charge tied to its acquisition of biotech company Terns Pharmaceuticals.

item.title: Can your tax preparer use AI without telling you? Some experts say IRS rules aren't clear
item.description: A debate is brewing among tax practitioners regarding whether using AI to prepare tax returns should require a disclosure to clients.
